title: Profile sensitivity INT8 vs FP8 lab demo - SparrowTech
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a focused Optimize console demo comparing INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles using SparrowTech's chat summarization workload. Discussion covered quality vs latency, recommended rollout strategy (canary by prompt set), metric targets, and next steps to run a 72-hour sandbox benchmark with customer prompts and SSO-enabled private test environment.
action_items: Alex Park - share sandbox instructions and cost estimate by 2026-05-22
Maya Chen - upload representative prompt set and 2500 sample conversations by 2026-05-25
Jamal Ortiz - prepare INT8/FP8 profile export and suggested evaluation metrics by 2026-05-26
next_steps: Share security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, KMS configuration)
Run small-scale latency sweep on customer-like payloads
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE); Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE); Sophie Nguyen (Redwood Product); Luis Fernandez (SE); Maya Chen (SparrowTech, ML Eng); Omar Singh (SparrowTech, Platform); Rhea Patel (SparrowTech, Head Product)
---
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, i'm alex and i'll run the high level flow, jamal will pick up the deep bench later. can folks do a quick round robin?
[00:10] Maya (SparrowTech): hi all, maya here, ml infra at sparrow, we're looking to cut generation latency for our summarization assistant and lower token costs without regressing quality too much.
[00:18] Omar (SparrowTech): omar, platform, mainly worried about private deployment and whether we can keep logs in our cloud region.
[00:24] Rhea (SparrowTech): rhea, product - timeline is end of q3 for rollout, success metric is <250ms p50 and no more than 2% drop in rouge/literary quality on core prompts.
[00:34] Alex: great, thanks. quick agenda: show Optimize console quantization profiles, run a quick INT8 vs FP8 sample, discuss tradeoffs and rollout path.
[00:42] Jamal (Redwood SE): i'll jump in around the 10 minute mark to show the lab, and we'll surface configs - batching, kv cache, prefix caching, and routing.
[00:50] 
[02:05] Alex: ok i'm sharing my screen. this is the Optimize tab in the Console — some customers call it "OptimiZe" in notes, so ignore that. first panel: profile catalog. you'll see two saved profiles we prepped: sparrow-default-int8 and sparrow-default-fp8.
[02:25] Maya: slight audio glitch, but i can see the screen now.
[02:30] Jamal: cool. the INT8 profile is aggressive quantization plus per-layer fallback on a few attention heads; FP8 keeps higher fidelity in dense layers. both use our KV prefix cache for repeated system prompts.
[02:45] Omar: are those profiles global or per-model?
[02:48] Jamal: per-model and per-deployment. you can pin a profile on Dedicated or in your Private control plane. for hosted we auto-route to compatible kernels.
[03:10] Alex: let's run a quick quality check. we have 30 sample transcripts that mimic your user flows — summarization of multi-paragraph email threads.
[03:22] [03:30] Jamal: starting the bench now. running both profiles sequentially on the same seed set to compare token generation and latency.
[03:45] [04:00] System noise / typing
[04:10] Jamal: first-pass results: INT8 p50 latency 180ms, p95 420ms; FP8 p50 230ms, p95 520ms. token usage roughly similar, INT8 shows 8-12% CPU/GPU utilization drop.
[04:35] Maya: what's the quality delta? we care about hallucination and summary coherence.
[04:40] Jamal: good question. we ran two automatic evals - rouge-l and a semantic similarity score. INT8 had a -1.8% delta on rouge-l on average, FP8 -0.4%. human spot checks (we did 5) flagged one instance from INT8 with mild brevity.
[04:58] Rhea: so INT8 gets you ~50ms p50 improvement but ~1.8% rouge drop, is that consistent across longer contexts?
[05:10] Jamal: it depends. for longer context (2k tokens) the delta narrows because caching helps; also INT8's attention head fallback reduces some loss but costs extra ops in those layers.
[05:30] 
[06:00] Alex: tradeoffs to consider: latency-sensitive path (low-latency chat) we recommend FP8 for critical prompts and INT8 for lower-risk background summarization. rollouts typically start with canary profile per prompt-tag.
[06:20] Omar: can you route by prompt tag? we have multiple teams using the same endpoint.
[06:25] Jamal: yes — routing policy supports per-route profile pinning and canary percentages. you can also route by token length, region, or customer tier.
[06:40] Maya: what about batching and prefetch? our traffic has lots of short bursts.
[06:45] Jamal: continuous batching works well for sustained load, for spiky traffic we recommend small-window batching plus prefix/KV caching for repeated system messages — that saves about 15-30% tokens on your pattern.
[07:05] 
[07:30] Sophie (Product): i'm going to open the evaluation dashboard — you'll see quality histograms and a sensitivity plot. this plot maps quality delta vs latency delta per prompt cluster.
[07:45] [08:00] Sophie: notice this cluster here (email-threads-long) — INT8 plotted at -1.6% quality and -20% latency; FP8 at -0.5% and -12% latency.
[08:20] Maya: are those human-annotated clusters or auto-clustered?
[08:25] Sophie: auto cluster first, you can attach human labels. we recommend a small human eval batch for important clusters.
[08:40] 
[09:15] Jamal: now i'll open the lab to show profile sensitivity sweep. we run an automated quant sweep across layers to generate a precision map, and then build a hybrid profile — some layers remain FP8 while others int8 — that's often the sweet spot.
[09:35] Omar: interesting, can you export that hybrid profile?
[09:40] Jamal: yes, exportable JSON plus we provide a diff view versus baseline. you can also import it into your private deployment.
[09:55] 
[10:30] Alex: quick security note — for Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM, audit logs go to your SIEM, and data-in-rest is customer-controlled.
[10:40] Rhea: we need logs to stay in eu-west only. is that supported?
[10:45] Alex: yes, region-level retention and residency supported for Private; hosted can be regionally pinned for enterprise tiers. we'll share the compliance pack.
[11:02] 
[11:20] Jamal: back to the bench — i pushed a hybrid profile (sparrow-hybrid-1). p50 195ms, p95 430ms, rouge delta -0.6% avg. that meets your 250ms p50 target with less than 1% quality drop.
[11:45] Maya: that looks promising. what's the expected cost delta?
[11:50] Jamal: rough calc: INT8 ~18% lower token compute cost, hybrid ~10% lower versus FP8 baseline. we'll provide a detailed cost model for your workload.
[12:10] 
[12:30] Omar: for the sandbox run, do you need us to provide data or can you generate synthetic?
[12:35] Alex: for realistic results we prefer your representative prompt set and 2-3 weeks of traffic sample; if that's sensitive you can de-identify or run the sandbox in your VPC with our private control plane.
[12:55] Maya: we can upload a de-id set of 2500 sessions.
[13:05] 
[13:30] Rhea: what's the rollout plan you recommend?
[13:35] Jamal: start with a canary on non-critical routes for 1-2 weeks, run the sandbox with a full pass of the eval suite, human review on top clusters, then ramp to 25/50/100% over 2-4 weeks. enable automatic rollback if metric drift > threshold.
[13:55] Maya: do you support A/B testing with our analytics?
[13:58] Sophie: yes we have integrations and webhooks for metric export; you can push logs to your analytics pipeline.
[14:12] 
[14:40] Alex: quick Q/A — Omar asked about private test environments and SSO. we support SAML/SSO and can spin up a dedicated sandbox in your VPC for the trial.
[14:58] Omar: good. also curious about model fallback if a profile fails.
[15:03] Jamal: automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or higher-precision profile is supported; you can set retry counts and prefer latency or fidelity during fallback.
[15:20] 
[15:50] Maya: i noticed one of the sample INT8 outputs had slightly shorter completions; can we tune length penalty or repetition penalty to mitigate?
[15:55] Jamal: yes, we can adjust sampling params and also pin more layers to higher precision to preserve generation length. we'll include those knobs in the sandbox config.
[16:20] 
[16:45] Alex: we're about out of time; quick recap: we'll run a 72-hour sandbox using your de-id prompts, Redwood will prepare the hybrid candidate profile and cost model, share security/compliance docs and sandbox instructions.
[17:05] Rhea: timeline — can we aim to start sandbox next week?
[17:10] Alex: yes, if prompts are uploaded by 2026-05-25 we can stand up sandbox by 2026-05-27.
[17:18] 
[17:30] Maya: one more thing — are there known issues with specific open models and INT8? we saw reports of repeat tokens.
[17:36] Jamal: some model families are more sensitive; our profile generator catches those patterns and either pins FP8 for that layer or uses attention head fallback. repeats can be mitigated by penalty tuning.
[17:55] 
[18:15] Luis (SE): i'll follow up with a README for the sandbox and sample config for the rollout.
[18:25] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and next steps.
[18:35] Omar: thanks, good session.
[18:40] End of recording
notes: Hybrid profile (sparrow-hybrid-1) hit target p50 under 250ms with <1% quality delta on sample set; customer to provide de-id prompts; Redwood to share security pack and cost model.
